> **What this document is.** Qualification *evidence*, not a qualification. A

> script can be that. What this removes is the part a quality reviewer should
> never have to establish by hand — which requirement is implemented by which

> Review starts from observed fact rather than from a claim.

> is ever rendered as a pass.

## Intended use

Controlled documents, their lifecycle and the records that evidence their control.

Surfaces in scope: `quality`, `qmp`

**Reading the impact column.** `direct` means the software itself affects the
integrity, authenticity or content of a regulated record, or decides who may act
on one. `indirect` means it supports that work without producing the record.
The distinction sets the assurance effort: a direct-impact requirement cannot be
discharged by inspection, and the gate refuses a registry that tries.

## Requirement detail

### URS-QMS-01 — The system shall serve and write controlled-document, training and change-control records only within the caller's organization, refusing any request that carries no organization context with HTTP 403.

**Intended use.** A quality lead opens the SOP register and the change-control log for their own company. Every controlled document, training acknowledgment and change record is a regulated record whose owner must be unambiguous; a cross-tenant read would put another company's effective SOPs and approvals in front of an auditor as though they were this company's.

**If it fails.** An unscoped or mis-scoped request returns another organization's qms_documents / qms_change_controls rows. The register then shows effective SOPs, approvers and training counts that belong to a different company, and an inspector or a QA decision treats them as this tenant's quality system.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** medium

> **Not yet qualified to the level this risk deserves.** The evidence cited

> **high**. Owed: an integration or end-to-end test that exercises this behaviour against the real route; the evidence cited today supports only medium assurance. Until that exists this
> requirement is declared and partially evidenced, not qualified, and
> VSR-LAUNCH-001 counts it against the package.

### URS-QMS-04 — The system shall write a 21 CFR Part 11 §11.10(e) audit row for every governed write in the /api/mdx/qms router and report in that response's meta.auditTrail whether the row persisted, rather than returning an identical response whether or not the record exists.

**Intended use.** Creating, editing, approving, revising, retiring a controlled document, acknowledging training, and raising, transitioning or linking a change are all audit-trail subjects. The caller and the surface must be able to tell a recorded governed action from an unrecorded one.

**If it fails.** The audit write fails (auditService.logAction resolves rather than rejecting on persistence failure) and the outcome is discarded. The document is approved, the change is transitioned, and the response is byte-identical to the audited case — so the only trace of the missing §11.10(e) record is a server log line, and the Part 11 export is silently incomplete.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** high

### URS-QMS-05 — The system shall advance a change control only along the declared lifecycle (proposed → under assessment → approved/rejected → in implementation → verification → closed, with verification also returnable to in implementation, and cancellation from proposed, under assessment, approved or in implementation) and shall refuse an undeclared transition with HTTP 409 rather than silently ignoring it.

**Intended use.** A change-control coordinator moves a change through ICH Q10 / EU GMP Annex 15 stages. The lifecycle is the control: a change must not reach implementation without assessment and approval, and a terminal change must not be reopened.

**If it fails.** A change is moved from 'closed' back to 'approved', or from 'proposed' straight to 'in_implementation'. The change-control log then shows an implemented change that was never impact-assessed or independently approved, and the stamps (approved_by, implemented_at, verified_at) no longer describe what happened.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** high

### URS-QMS-06 — The system shall refuse, with HTTP 422, any change-control approval performed by the same user who proposed the change, and shall stamp approved_by and approved_at only on an accepted approval.

**Intended use.** Independent review is the segregation-of-duties control ICH Q10 and Part 11 expect on a change approval. The person who raised the change may not be the person who approves it.

**If it fails.** A proposer approves their own change. The change-control record then carries approved_by equal to proposed_by, and an inspection finds a governed change that passed no independent review while the record asserts that it did.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** high

### URS-QMS-07 — The system shall record cross-references from a change control to its deviations, CAPAs, validation records, SOPs and controlled documents and shall serve them on GET /api/mdx/qms/changes/:id and /changes/:id/links; the change-control log's expanded row renders links only when the rows it was given carry them, which the register read does not supply.

**Intended use.** A change is only defensible with the deviations that triggered it, the CAPAs it addresses and the validation it requires attached to it. A reviewer expands a change in the log to see exactly those, without leaving the surface.

**If it fails.** A link is dropped or an expanded change renders no cross-references although rows exist. A reviewer concludes the change touches no validated process, and an implemented change ships with its revalidation obligation invisible.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** medium

### URS-QMS-09 — The system shall report an unreadable QMS read as unavailable and never as an empty result: the change-control KPI row shall render "Change-log totals are unavailable" in place of zeroes, the quality-plan register shall render a distinct error state separate from "no quality plans yet", the state published to AnA shall say the change log could not be read rather than that it is empty, and an AnA open-change directive shall be refused while the read is failed and held (not failed) while it is still loading.

**Intended use.** A quality lead must never read a failed fetch as an all-clear. "Zero open changes" and "the change log did not load" lead to opposite decisions before an inspection, and AnA must not assert an empty register on the strength of a failed read.

**If it fails.** A 500, an expired token or a body the client cannot adapt renders as a row of zeroes and an empty register. The lead reports "nothing overdue, nothing awaiting approval" to management, and AnA repeats it, while the real register is unread.

**CSA impact.** indirect · **assurance level achieved** medium

### URS-QMS-10 — The system shall never substitute example QMS content for tenant data: fixture SOPs, training-completion counts and change records shall appear only when sample mode is explicitly enabled, which is force-disabled in production builds; the standing 'Sample data — not your project' marker is rendered from the document/change register's own source, so a panel whose own source is empty can render its fixture while the marker is suppressed.

**Intended use.** An effective-SOP list and a read-and-understood training record are exactly what an auditor asks to see. A user must always be able to tell canonical example content from their own regulated data.

**If it fails.** An empty tenant, an expired token or a failed fetch causes fixture rows asserting status 'effective' with effective dates, and training counts such as "47 of 47", to render unmarked. A filing or inspection-readiness decision is taken against example data presented as the company's own.

**CSA impact.** indirect · **assurance level achieved** medium

### URS-QMS-12 — The system shall list, create and activate quality-management plans against the organization-scoped quality API behind a tenant-context gate, and shall show a selected plan's completeness, section gate-level split and factor risk profile only when the full dashboard payload is present.

**Intended use.** A QMP defines the gate levels and risk factors every other governed document is validated against, so a quality lead needs to see which plan is active and what it enforces before activating it.

**If it fails.** A partial dashboard body renders as a populated panel, so a freshly created plan with no sections shows "0 hard gates" as though it enforced nothing, and a lead activates it believing the gates are configured.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** medium

### URS-QMS-90 — The system shall return a visitor with no session from the QMS controlled documents surface `quality` to sign-in, and shall render that surface only once a session is established.

**Intended use.** A regulatory user reaches QMS controlled documents through an authenticated session. The record this surface exposes is a regulated one, so an unauthenticated visitor must be returned to sign-in rather than shown any part of it.

**If it fails.** The surface renders for a visitor with no session, exposing a regulated record to an unidentified person and breaking the attribution every audit entry depends on.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** high
